question.problem:
The curvature of the plane curve $r(t)=t\,i+\frac{1}{t+1}\,j$ is given by 

$$
κ(t)=\frac{2(t+1)^{3}}{\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}},\,t>-1.
$$

 
What is the missing part of the expression?
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{|{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)|}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)=\frac{1}{t+1}.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =1,\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =-\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =0,\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =\frac{2}{(t+1)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{|1\cdot \frac{2}{(t+1)^{3}}-0\cdot (-\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}})|}{{({1}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}})}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{|\frac{2}{(t+1)^{3}}|}{{(1+\frac{1}{(t+1)^{4}})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{|\frac{2}{(t+1)^{3}}|}{\sqrt{{[\frac{(t+1)^{4}+1}{(t+1)^{4}}]}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{2(t+1)^{6}}{|(t+1)^{3}|\sqrt{{((t+1)^{4}+1)}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{2(t+1)^{6}}{(t+1)^{3}\sqrt{{((t+1)^{4}+1)}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{2(t+1)^{3}}{\sqrt{{((t+1)^{4}+1)}^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we removed the absolute value because $t>-1.$
